source_read_scope: Complete IIOKitDeviceLifetime.cs; narrow owner worker/shutdown/close and bridge-forwarding context only. Source inspection, no runtime or native execution.

evidence.conclusion: CreateDevice composes IORegistryEntryIDMatching, IOServiceGetMatchingService and IOHIDDeviceCreate; it throws PlatformApiException on missing service/device and releases the temporary service in finally. This is not a one-call forwarding operation.

OpenDevice delegates to status-returning OpenDeviceResult and translates nonzero status to PlatformApiException; CloseDeviceChecked compares native status with zero. Existing option values/signatures and status interpretation are unchanged.

Feature reports/callback registrations forward native operations; ReleaseCFObject forwards CFRelease, while run-loop mode creation and integer-property lookup use managed helpers. Native boundaries remain visible and interceptable.

The owner worker invokes admitted work before Close, shutdown sets stopping and returns its shared close task, and checked close/CF release precede registration release. Failed unproven release retains the rooted owner/claim. Scheduling, drain and release ordering belong to that owner, not to the seam interface.

The separate FIDO bridge forwards creation/open/metadata/release helpers to the production lifetime implementation; its report/native-input boundary remains separate. No claim that substituting this interface alone exercises every FIDO route.

testability_limit: Injected implementations let tests intercept native-lifetime and feature-report operations and inspect owner ordering. This return claims no fresh test execution, native drain proof, deployed-library qualification or hardware behavior.
